# 3ngram v1.6.3

Patch: native MCP clients such as Claude Code can authorize again, and the
mail transport moves off a nodemailer release with a high-severity advisory.

v1.6.2 was tagged but never published: the release image scan rejected
`nodemailer@9.0.1`, so that version number is burned and this release carries
its content. `@3ngram/core` 0.11.2, `@3ngram/schema` 0.9.1 and `@3ngram/db`
0.10.2 reach npm for the first time here.

## Changes

- **Loopback redirect URIs match on any port** (#208). Claude Code registers
  through a Client ID Metadata Document whose `redirect_uris` are
  `http://localhost/callback` and `http://127.0.0.1/callback` with no port,
  then presents `redirect_uri=http://localhost:<ephemeral port>/callback`,
  because a native client cannot know its loopback port before it binds one.
  `/oauth/authorize` matched redirect URIs byte-exactly, so every such login
  ended in `400 invalid_client` with `reason=redirect_uri_mismatch`. A
  presented URI now also matches when a registered URI is `http` on the same
  loopback host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, never cross-matched) with
  an identical path and query; only the port may differ, on either side. The
  requested URI, port included, is what the 302 targets, what the
  authorization code is bound to, and what `/oauth/token` compares against.
  `https` URIs, non-loopback `http`, and any path or query difference stay
  byte-exact.

- **`http://[::1]` is a registrable loopback redirect.** `redirectUriSchema`
  admitted plain `http` only for `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`; the IPv6
  loopback literal now joins them for DCR and CIMD alike. The hostname check
  runs against the parser-canonicalised host, so every spelling of `::1` is
  accepted and no other address is.

- **Redirect URIs must use RFC 3986 characters.** Registration rejects a
  redirect URI carrying a character the URI grammar never allows unencoded
  (a backslash above all, which the WHATWG parser reads as `/`). The rule is
  defined once in `@3ngram/schema` as `hasForbiddenUriCharacter` and reused by
  the loopback matcher, so a registration predating this release that carries
  such a character keeps byte-exact matching and gains no port relaxation.

- **nodemailer 9.0.1 → 9.1.1** (#211). Clears GHSA-2x7j-588g-ccc2 (high,
  quadratic address-list parsing enabling remote denial of service) and three
  medium advisories on recipient-domain validation and `resolveContent()`
  access controls.

No migrations. Schema head stays at `0036_triage_armed_at`. Both triage
mechanisms (`SESSION_CLOSER_ENABLED`, `THREENGRAM_STOP_NUDGE`) remain
**default-off** pending the #166 validation bar.
